findings.title: Reassigning exit code 4 silently changes CLI contract
findings.body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE was changed from 4 to 3, and the previously-used value 4 is now repurposed as FEATURE_DISABLED. Any existing automation/scripts built against the earlier shipped behavior (where exit code 4 meant 'rolling upgrade not possible, recreate required') will now silently misinterpret a 'feature disabled' result as 'recreate required', or vice versa. Even though update-compatibility is a preview feature, this is a behavior-changing contract break for the exit codes documented in docs/guides/server/update-compatibility.adoc and should be called out explicitly (e.g., in release notes) rather than silently swapped as a side effect of this PR.

findings.title: Missing test for feature-disabled path on the 'check' subcommand
findings.body: testFeatureNotEnabled only exercises UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.NAME without the rolling-updates feature enabled. The same feature-gating logic was also added to UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() (in UpdateCompatibilityCheck.java), but there is no corresponding test verifying that running 'check' without the feature enabled prints the expected error and exits with CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED. This leaves part of the newly introduced gating logic untested.

findings.title: ROLLING_UPDATES feature auto-enables with the generic 'preview' profile
findings.body: ROLLING_UPDATES is declared as Type.PREVIEW rather than Type.PREVIEW_DISABLED_BY_DEFAULT. Per Profile.isEnabledByDefault(), any Type.PREVIEW feature is automatically turned on whenever the server-wide profile is set to PREVIEW (e.g. via a general '--profile=preview' or env var toggle), without the operator/administrator explicitly opting into 'rolling-updates'. Since this flag changes default update/rollback behavior for update-compatibility commands and the Operator's update strategy, silently enabling it alongside unrelated preview features could cause unexpected behavior changes for users who only intended to try other preview features.

findings.title: Operator enforcement of rolling-updates feature flag not verifiable in this change set
findings.body: The new CAUTION block states 'While on preview stage, the feature rolling-updates must be enabled. Otherwise, the {project_name} Operator will fail.' However, none of the files included in this PR implement an operator-side check that fails when the update stanza is used without the feature enabled (only the CLI update-compatibility commands gained such a check in AbstractUpdatesCommand/UpdateCompatibilityCheck/Metadata). If the enforcement logic lives in a file not touched by this PR, that's fine, but reviewers should confirm the Operator actually performs this validation; otherwise the documentation overstates the current behavior and the CR update stanza being used with the feature disabled could silently fall back to unintended behavior instead of failing as documented.
